newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - More gains seen if dlr ends above 114 yen.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - More gains seen if dlr ends above 114 yen.

text.p: A dollar close above 114 yen on Monday could pave the way for further gains near term, according to chartists.
The U.S. currency last closed above 114 yen in April 1993.
"If we're able to get a New York close above 114 tonight, it looks extremely bullish," said Martin Autotte, a technical analyst at CIBC Wood Gundy in Montreal.
Autotte said he could easily see the dollar hitting 115 yen and possibly higher in the week ahead.
However, he said the dollar may run into resistance at 115 yen, if only because it will be a key psychological level.
The dollar surged on Monday to 114.39 yen, a fresh 42-month high and then slid slightly lower to trade around 114.14/19 yen in afternoon dealings. The U.S. currency had opened at 114.30/35 yen.
Scott Siller, a senior technical analyst at MCM CurrencyWatch, said a dollar close above 114 yen might keep the tone firm and possibly open the way for a further extension higher.
Yet Siller also warned the dollar rally may be running out of steam.

Siller noted the dollar has been in a bull channel since September 1995. Based on the weekly chart, Siller said the maximum the channel could extend to should be 114.75 yen before the dollar pulls back.
"So, I think, the (dollar's) upside is limited from here," he added.
Siller also emphasized the important role gains in mark/yen have played in the dollar/yen rally.
The German unit traded around 75.17/18 yen in the afternoon.
Siller pegged solid mark/yen resistance at 75.25.
"I don't see it getting much above 75.25 or 75.50 ..., which could make dollar/yen weaken as well," Siller said.
Furthermore, he said dollar/mark may sell off if dollar/yen does.
The U.S. currency traded near 1.5194/99 marks in late dealings, down from 1.5220/25 marks at the open.

CIBC's Autotte said a break below support at 1.5160 marks, last week's low, could leave the dollar targeting 1.5042 marks, a 50 percent Fibonnaci retracement of the move higher from 1.4625 in late July to 1.5460 in October.
